question.text: Options on Goods may be priced higher than Options on Futures because:

answer.text: Spot markets lack Daily Price Limits (DPL), leading to higher volatility, and writers face direct delivery obligations
Options on Goods have longer expiry periods
Commodity exchanges charge higher fees for Options on Goods
Options on Goods cannot be offset before expiry

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook gives two pricing reasons: (1) spot markets do not have Daily Price Limits like futures, so higher volatility increases option pricing; and (2) writers face direct delivery/payment obligations, increasing risk and the premium they demand. The Trap: Although the workbook notes that Options on Goods normally have a longer tenure than Options on Futures, that tenure difference is not given as the pricing reason. Exchange fees are not cited as a factor, and Options on Goods can in fact be offset before expiry. Note: Keep the tenure comparison and the pricing reasons distinct - only the volatility-from-no-DPL and the direct delivery/payment exposure are listed as the reasons for the premium gap.
